name: Genetics, Genomics and Development (GGD) PhD
summary: Cornell's PhD field in genetics, genomics and development, with more than 60 faculty from 15 departments. Students complete three research rotations in the first year.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The Graduate School's list of revised deadlines gives December 1, 2026 for Genetics (PhD), and the department's admissions page says the deadline for fall admission is December 1, with no spring admission. The university catalog entry still shows November 16, which the Graduate School says its revised list supersedes. No time of day is stated.

timeline.interviews: A select number of applicants are invited to interview at on-campus Recruitment events in March. Those who can't attend, for example some international applicants living outside the US, are offered Zoom interviews.
timeline.decisions: Admissions decisions are made by early to mid-March, once all interviews have taken place.

english.note: All applicants must show English proficiency with TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic scores unless they meet one of the Graduate School's exemptions (for example, a bachelor's degree from an accredited US college). Duolingo and other tests aren't accepted. Scores must be valid on the application deadline (two years from the test date). The Graduate School says the minimums it publishes apply to Summer and Fall 2026 admission only and are expected to rise for Fall 2027, and its page said to check back in mid-October for an update, so no minimums are listed here. The department's page lists TOEFL section minimums of Reading 20, Writing 20, Listening 15 and Speaking 22, and an IELTS overall score of 7.0 or higher. Self-report your scores in the application; official scores are needed before any offer.

applicationFee.note: Nonrefundable, and the same for international applicants. The Graduate School can waive it in exceptional cases of financial hardship and lists economic conditions in your home country among the factors it weighs. Requests are approved only for applicants to fully funded doctoral or research master's programs, or those who will submit a FAFSA. Ask on the payment page, and submit your application at least three business days before the deadline. The department says fields can't issue waivers; the Graduate School also considers requests from pipeline-program participants.

requirements.note: Applications are judged as a whole: grades, the statement of purpose and, especially, the letters of recommendation. Statements run up to 1,200 words (academic) and 1,000 words (personal). Official transcripts aren't needed to apply, but upload transcripts from every college attended, even without a degree. A résumé or CV is required for GGD. BMCB and GGD applicants pick the program that best fits their current research interests, and students can move between the two at the end of the first year if their interests change.

funding.note: All matriculating students receive full support for the time typically needed to finish (5 to 6 years) while making satisfactory progress: a stipend, full tuition and individual medical insurance. In later years, support generally comes from graduate research or teaching assistantships, and many students win their own fellowships. The pages give no stipend amount; the Graduate School's minimum for assistantships in 2026-27 is $36,684 for 9 months or $48,912 for 12 months (2027-28 rates aren't posted yet).
